visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short black hair and glasses, wearing a black shirt, is framed in a medium shot against a background consisting of a macro close-up of orange salmon roe. He speaks directly to the camera with an expressive face and hand gestures. (2) The scene cuts to a screen displaying a digital copy of a research paper abstract from PNAS titled 'The entities enabling scientific fraud at scale...'. Text and author names are clearly visible. (3) Returning to the man, he continues his explanation, now holding a blue pen and using it to emphasize his points. The lighting is bright and centered on him. (4) A series of four statistical bar charts appear, illustrating growth in total articles, retractions, PubPeer comments, and short turnaround times from 2010 to 2020. (5) Back to the man, who gestures with his hands to mimic the 'paper mill' production process. (6) A complex network diagram is displayed, showing interconnected nodes of various sizes representing editors and authors, with colored lines indicating different types of flags or relationships. (7) Returning to the man, he maintains a serious expression. (8) A multi-colored line graph shows the exponential growth of 'Paper mill products' compared to regular scientific articles, projected towards 2030. (9) Final shot of the man, looking slightly concerned then inquisitive as he asks a concluding question.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Slogan]: 加入泛糰會員 一起撐開腦洞. [Slogan]: 論文造假的龐大暗組織現形. [Subtitle]: 論文的參考文獻出現了民明書房. [Logo]: Pansci. (2) [Subtitle]: 如果你還沒看到，可能也快了，因為更扯的事情正在發生. (3) [Subtitle]: 一篇發表在《美國國家科學院院刊 (PNAS)》上的研究揭開了學術圈最噁心的內幕. (4) [Subtitle]: 一個全球化的科學造假產業鏈，而且他的成長速度足以把正規科學的臉壓在地上摩擦. (5) [Subtitle]: 揭露這個黑暗組織的是來自美國西北大學的一群鍵盤柯南. (6) [Subtitle]: 他們的第一步是建立史上最全的論文戶口名簿，把全球主流學術資料庫像 Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed 等全部抓下來. (7) [Subtitle]: 建立了一個包含數億篇論文的超巨大資料庫. (8) [Subtitle]: 接著他們匯入了所有的犯罪紀錄跟黑函，也就是全球最大的撤稿資料庫 Retraction Watch 還有學術界最愛的論壇 PubPeer 上所有的吐槽文. (9) [Subtitle]: 哪篇論文被罵、被抓包，一清二楚. (10) [Subtitle]: 最聰明的一步是他們鎖定了像 PLOS ONE 這種會公布每篇文章經手編輯的期刊. (11) [Subtitle]: 畫出了作者與編輯的攻受關係網. (12) [Subtitle]: 看是不是有特定的作者老是把文章丟給特定的編輯，然後那些文章又特別容易出包被撤稿. (13) [Subtitle]: 最後他們直接用軟體比對上萬篇論文，抓一圖多用的複製貼上鐵證. (14) [Subtitle]: 甚至還用了網站時光機 Wayback Machine 去追蹤一個叫做 ARDA 的論文掮客組織的犯罪軌跡. (15) [Subtitle]: 在收集了這麼多證據之後，整個黑暗組織的輪廓就浮現了. (16) [Subtitle]: 首先有負責生產的論文工廠 paper mills 專門用 AI 生成圖表、瞎掰數據、大量產製假論文. (17) [Subtitle]: 接著有負責銷售的掮客 brokers 他們會把論文的作者掛名當成精品包一樣，價高者得. (18) [Subtitle]: 他們還有內鬼，會跟某些期刊的編輯勾結，讓你下單的論文保證刊登. (19) [Subtitle]: 這個集團超狡猾，一旦合作的期刊被抓包、被除名 de-indexing 他們就立刻換一本. (20) [Subtitle]: 這招叫期刊跳躍 journal hopping 比政客換腦還快. (21) [Subtitle]: 這問題非常嚴重，數據顯示這些假論文的數量每 1.5 年就翻一倍. (22) [Subtitle]: 而老實的科學家辛辛苦苦做的真研究，要 15 年才能翻一倍. (23) [Subtitle]: 有參與的科學家表示這大概是他這輩子做過最讓人沮喪的研究了. (24) [Subtitle]: 更可怕的是這些造假的論文如果沒有被抓出來，未來就會被當成科學事實拿去訓練下一代的 AI 模型. (25) [Subtitle]: 如果 AI 學的都是這些垃圾，那我們就真的完蛋了. (26) [Subtitle]: 哈？你說你最相信的就是民明書房跟泛科學新聞？

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A mature male voice begins speaking with high articulation and a moderate-to-fast speech rate. He sounds professional yet engaging. There is a low-volume ambient Lo-fi BGM with a steady 4/4 beat. Studio-quality silence fills the gaps between his words. (2) As he introduces the research study, his tone becomes more serious and emphatic. Subtle 'whoosh' sounds are audible during scene transitions. The music remains steady, providing a neutral background. (3) The vocal intensity increases when describing 'paper mills' and 'brokers,' using sharp intonation to highlight specific technical terms. (4) The audio maintains a high Signal-to-Noise Ratio, ensuring that every syllable of the dense information-heavy script is clear. (5) In the final moments, the speaker's tone shifts to a slightly more inquisitive and lighthearted one as he concludes with a playful reference, followed by the music fading out cleanly.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Linear: Hook -> Explanation of Study Methodology -> Disclosure of Findings -> Future Risks -> Conclusion/CTA
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate viewers about a significant PNAS study that exposed the vast and growing industry of scientific fraud, including 'paper mills' and deceptive editorial practices, highlighting the threat these pose to the integrity of science and AI training.

The juxtaposition of a professional narrator against a colorful, slightly abstract background (ikura) creates a distinctive visual style common in modern Chinese-language science communication channels.
